  name: "Dynamic Few-Shot (k-NN)",
  objective: "Improve generalization by dynamically selecting the most relevant examples from a corpus instead of using a fixed few-shot prompt.",
  mechanism: "COMPACT v2 ENTRY — legacy-synthesized. The mechanism text below is the legacy corpus description, programmatically normalized: fabricated/unverified model references removed, citation-like brackets neutralized, claimed efficacy [ESTIMATE] figures labeled ESTIMATE. No known pseudo-mechanism vocabulary detected. This entry is NOT validated against current published research — treat every mechanism and claimed efficacy [ESTIMATE] claim as unverified legacy material until full v2 enhancement lands. \n\nMaintain a library of (input, output) examples embedded into a vector space. For a new query, compute its embedding and retrieve the top-k most similar past examples (k-NN). Insert these as few-shot demonstrations into the prompt before the query. This provides task-specific guidance that adapts to the query distribution.\\n\\nCore pipeline:\\n1. Example corpus\\n   - Store historical (input, output, metadata) pairs from real usage or curated datasets.\\n   - Periodically clean, de-duplicate, and label examples with domain, task type, and quality scores.\\n\\n2. Embedding & index\\n   - Use a sentence/document embedding model (often distinct from the main LLM) to encode each example input, or joint input+output representation.\\n   - Build a vector index (ANN: HNSW, IVF, ScaNN, etc.) for efficient k-NN retrieval at scale.\\n\\n3. Query processing\\n   - Encode the incoming query into the same embedding space.\\n   - Retrieve top-k examples; optionally filter by domain, recency, or quality.\\n   - Optionally apply diversity constraints (e.g., MMR) to prevent near-duplicates.\\n\\n4. Prompt assembly\\n   - Prepend selected examples as few-shot demonstrations in a consistent format.\\n   - Then append the new query and an instruction such as 'Using the patterns above, answer the following question.'\\n\\n5. Feedback loop\\n   - Capture model outputs and user feedback.\\n   - Promote high-quality new pairs back into the example corpus, keeping the system adaptive over time.\\n\\nThis dynamic few-shot approach automatically adapts prompts as the distribution of queries and the underlying knowledge base evolve.",
  mitigation: "Mitigates 'Prompt Staleness' where static demonstrations no longer match current queries. Reduces hallucinations by anchoring to similar real cases.\\n\\nAdditional mitigations (2024–2026 deployments):\\n• Reduces domain drift: as new product features, regulations, or workflows appear, new examples enter the corpus and begin to influence retrieved shots without manually rewriting system prompts.\\n• Mitigates style inconsistency by conditioning on representative examples from a specific customer tone/brand segment.\\n• Lowers chance of logically inconsistent answers in narrow domains, since retrieved examples encode domain-specific constraints and edge cases.\\n• Supports lower-capacity models (7–13B) by giving them explicit task patterns, partially compensating for limited parameter capacity.",
